title: Upscaling and tiling math
hook: How ComfyUI cuts an image into tiles, why a ramp hides the seam, and why tiled decoding saves memory but costs 3.77 times the work.

verified.claim: Tile starts are range(0, D - O, S - O) when D > S, cut off at the border.
decode_tiled_ decodes three tilings and averages them, for image latents.
ImageUpscaleWithModel starts at tile 512, overlap 32, halves on running out of memory, and gives up under 128.
The lab's tile plan and ramp follow those functions and ran on a toy decoder.
The tile play's starts for a side of 1024 match the lab.
Both graphs pass validate_prompt with file menus skipped.

unchecked: Seam errors come from a toy decoder with fixed random weights and zero padding. They don't measure a real VAE or upscaler.
The factor 3.77 assumes the decoder's cost grows with positions, which is only roughly true.
The lab doesn't compare resize methods. Whether latent or pixel upscaling looks better isn't measured here.
